answer: The catalogue should not assert a direct 'learned repertoire from' relationship between the granduncle and grandnephew as a primitive fact. CRM has no property for a direct interpersonal teaching/learning relation, and the SIG itself confronted this exact case (a ULAN 'student of'/'teacher of' pair) in Issue 256 and closed it without adopting any such property into CRMBase, deferring it to a never-realised 'CRMsoc' extension. Instead, each of the forty dated tapes should be catalogued as evidence of its own E7 Activity (a teaching/performance session), with P11 had participant linking that activity to both E21 Person instances (granduncle and grandnephew). The relationship the archive wants to record -- that the grandnephew learned his repertoire from his granduncle -- is then a derived reading of the recurring co-participation pattern across the forty activities, not a separate assertion the model makes for you: P11's own scope note says shared participation 'is most likely an indication of... acquaintance and interaction' but 'does not imply any causal relationship'. This matches the Minimality principle -- CRM deliberately does not declare shortcut properties for relations that are derivable from the primitive event pattern -- so the honest recommendation is: document the sessions, and let the teaching relationship be inferred by chaining them.

rejected_alternatives.option: A direct 'teacher of / student of' property between E21 Person instances
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Issue 256 (closed 2017-10-10) shows the SIG discussing exactly this relation (ULAN's 'student of'/'teacher of' pair) and explicitly declining to add it to CRMBase, calling it out-of-scope pending a hypothetical 'CRMsoc' extension -- which does not exist among the indexed family models (search.py concept CRMsoc: 'No such concept').

rejected_alternatives.option: E74 Group (P107 has current or former member / P143 joined / P144 joined with)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: In thread t0834, Martin Doerr argues E74 Group presumes members capable of 'acting as one' actor; a teacher and pupil do not meet that unity criterion, which is why the same thread proposed (but never adopted) a separate 'relationship group' subclass of E28/P89 instead of reusing E74.

Concept dossier and thread t0225 ('family relations') show this property, and the CRM's person-relation pattern generally, are anchored to E67 Birth -- a biological/legal parentage event -- not to a pattern of repeated teaching sessions; there is no analogous shortcut for transmitted skill or repertoire.
